notes: Bankfull width-to-depth ratio; both over-widened (very high) and incised (very low) degrade condition. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.

Log relative bed stability; departure from the reference core in EITHER direction departs from reference (negative excess fines, positive an armored, sediment-starved bed, the classic below-impoundment failure). The pilot's rising direction scored armored beds 1.0 and left Sediment continuity blind to its textbook failure mode. Two-sided form is an owner decision at the adversarial review gate, 2026-08-21.
Log mean substrate diameter; coarser substrate generally better, but valley-type dependent.
Large woody debris volume per 100 m; higher is better.
Percent fast-water (riffle/run) habitat; more generally better for many biota. Ecoregion-dependent.
Percent sand and fines; higher indicates fine-sediment loading (worse).
Residual pool depth per 100 m; deeper residual pools generally better habitat.
Channel sinuosity; higher generally indicates a more natural planform.

Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.
Mean bankfull height; both incision (very high banks) and over-widening (very low) depart from reference. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.
Mid-channel canopy density; higher shading generally better for thermal/light regime.
Riparian canopy plus mid-layer plus ground cover; higher is better.
Percent embeddedness; higher means interstitial spaces filled with fines (worse).
Natural fish cover; higher is better.

Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.

Watershed wetland (%), woody plus herbaceous, both classes required; wetlands store surface water and attenuate flow peaks. EASI scores Surface water storage on the same sum (method watershed-wetland-extent).
Mean watershed elevation; physiographic scaling context. Predictor only.
Mean annual precipitation (1981-2010 normal); scaling/climate context, not a condition indicator. Predictor only.
Mean annual runoff; scaling/climate context, not a condition indicator. Predictor only.
Reach channel slope class. Breakpoints 0.5 and 2 percent are fixed constants.
Mean watershed elevation class. Breakpoints 300 and 1000 m are fixed constants.

ChannelSlopeClass.notes: Reach channel slope class. Breakpoints 0.5 and 2 percent are fixed constants.
ChannelSlopeClass.rationale: Channel slope controls stream power, substrate sorting and channel type. 0.5 and 2 percent are the conventional low gradient, moderate and steep breaks used in Rosgen-family and Montgomery-Buffington channel typing. National median slope is near 0.13 percent, so this ladder is eligible in roughly half of L3 ecoregions; it is screened where it qualifies and excluded with a recorded reason where it does not.

ElevationClass.notes: Mean watershed elevation class. Breakpoints 300 and 1000 m are fixed constants.
ElevationClass.rationale: Elevation proxies thermal regime, precipitation phase and growing season length. 300 and 1000 m are conventional lowland, upland and montane breaks. Within a single ecoregion this often collapses to two populated classes, which the eligibility screen handles.

function_coverage_exceptions.justification: Every candidate metric for this function was withheld. The scored candidates are benthic total taxa richness and native fish taxa richness, and native non-tolerant fish taxa richness was also tested under Pre-registration III. Too few comparable least-disturbed stations carry them in this ecoregion or in its Level II and Level I parents. On comparable national donors the strongest result was native non-tolerant fish taxa richness on distance-matched donors, which reached promising: its class calls agreed with reference in 16 of 19 evaluation regions with no systematic promotion, but its recovered thresholds fell inside the true answer's uncertainty in only 9 of 19, against the 13 required to validate. No modeled expectation passed validation under the extrapolation this ecoregion requires. Ohio EPA's ecoregional biocriteria, the nearest applicable published criterion, were checked on 2026-09-21 and are not usable here on three independent grounds. They set thresholds on composite indices (the fish Index of Biotic Integrity, the Modified Index of well-being, and the Invertebrate Community Index) rather than on taxa richness, so applying one to a richness count would compare different quantities. Those indices are computed under Ohio EPA's own field protocol against metric lines calibrated on Ohio reference sites, and the NRSA archive carries no index column and cannot derive one. They are Ohio water quality standards keyed to a per-waterbody use designation, while 26 of this ecoregion's 51 stations lie in Indiana. No suitable basis was found among the sources evaluated, which is not a finding that this function cannot be scored. No curve was forced and the function is reported as unassessed, so the ecosystem condition index is stated as an interval.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 16 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a parent ecoregion, stating the level and the transfer risk. 2 carry the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds no stream clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 2 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. Too few comparable least-disturbed stations carry this metric in this ecoregion or in its Level II and Level I parents. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 17 comparable national donors carry this metric, but borrowed donors did not pass the recovery test for it, so they are not shown to transfer to this ecoregion. Modeled reference: The fitted expectation did not pass the recovery test for this metric. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

phab_BFWD_RAT.methodContext: At each transect, measure the bankfull width and the bankfull height above the water surface, and the thalweg depth. The value is the mean bankfull width divided by the mean bankfull depth (bankfull height plus thalweg depth).
